headline: Walk away. The screen locks. Your jobs keep running.
summary: A discreet menu bar utility that watches one trusted Apple Watch or iPhone. When you walk away past a short delay, WalkAway locks the screen. It does not sleep the Mac.
differentiator: macOS can unlock with Apple Watch. It does not lock when you leave. WalkAway fills that gap — without killing encodes, downloads, or renders.
featuresSubtitle: One toggle. One trusted device. Lock the screen, never the machine.

features.title: Lock, do not sleep
features.text: The lock screen comes up. CPU and processes stay up. WalkAway never calls sleep.

features.title: One trusted BLE device
features.text: Pick your Apple Watch or iPhone. WalkAway measures RSSI against a threshold you set.

features.title: Away delay, lock once
features.text: Away must last the delay (default 8 seconds) before lock. One lock per absence. Coming back clears the latch.

features.title: Arm and Disarm
features.text: Armed evaluates presence. Disarmed never locks from walking away. Lock Now works either way.

features.title: No auto-unlock
features.text: WalkAway does not type your password. Return uses system Unlock with Apple Watch, Touch ID, or password.

features.title: Privacy-friendly
features.text: No accounts, no tracking, no password stored. Bluetooth is used only to measure your device.

howSubtitle: Presence in, lock screen out. Jobs never stop.

how.title: Pick a device
how.text: Open Preferences and choose your Apple Watch. Armed turns on automatically.

how.title: Walk away
how.text: When the signal stays weaker than the threshold past the delay, WalkAway locks once.

how.title: Come back
how.text: Unlock with Watch or Touch ID — that is macOS, not WalkAway. The next leave can lock again.

quickStartSubtitle: From install to an armed lock in a few minutes.

quickStart.title: Install
quickStart.text: Download the DMG, drag WalkAway to Applications, and open it.

quickStart.title: Allow Bluetooth
quickStart.text: macOS will ask to use Bluetooth. Allow it so WalkAway can see your Watch.

quickStart.title: Pick your Watch
quickStart.text: Open Preferences, select the device, set the delay if you want. Armed is on.

quickStart.title: Walk away once
quickStart.text: Leave the desk. After the delay the lock screen should be up. ffmpeg should still be running.

faq.question: Does WalkAway sleep the Mac?
faq.answer: No. It locks the screen. Builds, downloads, and renders keep running.

faq.question: Does it unlock when I come back?
faq.answer: No. Unlock is the system: Apple Watch, Touch ID, or password. WalkAway never stores your password.

faq.question: Why Apple Watch instead of iPhone?
faq.answer: iPhone BLE addresses can change. Apple Watch is the reliable pick. AirPods can appear in the list too.

faq.question: Why does the first lock ask for System Events?
faq.answer: WalkAway locks through System Events. macOS asks once. WalkAway does not write TCC.db or flip Privacy switches for you.

faq.question: Is my data collected?
faq.answer: No. No accounts, no tracking. Settings live in a local JSON file.

faq.question: How is this different from SessionGuard?
faq.answer: SessionGuard keeps a session awake. WalkAway locks when you leave. Same catalog, opposite job.

faq.question: How do I update?
faq.answer: Use Check for Updates… in the WalkAway menu. The first install is still this site’s DMG.

install: Allow Bluetooth, pick your Watch in Preferences
downloadNotice: Free to use — including for businesses.
